what_happened: Dispatch's headline cost evidence for Gate 22 (lint-shellcheck.sh, claimed 542s/40% of total) and its individual lint timings do not reproduce on an idle machine: a live re-measurement (uptime load 0.6-2.2, 24 cores) found lint-shellcheck.sh at 75.9s (not 542s, ~7x faster) with 0 findings (not 2), while three other named lints were idle-SLOWER than their contended figures (lint-scoped-commit-boundary.sh 67.0s vs 40.5s claimed; lint-directory-pathspec-boundary.sh 22.8s vs 12.9s claimed; lint-task-lookup-adoption.sh 21.4s vs 12.6s claimed). Direction of drift is inconsistent, ruling out uniform contention inflation. Four xargs -P parallelization shapes were tested live against lint-shellcheck.sh's corpus: three batched shapes (-P24-n20, -P4-n96, -P8-n48) were all SLOWER than sequential; only true one-process-per-file (-P24-n1) won, at ~1.5x not the dispatch's implied ~15x. RECOMMENDATION: re-derive the gate cost model from fresh idle --only-gate-scoped measurements before finalizing registry scheduling/dependency design; scope shellcheck parallelization to one-process-per-file dispatch only, budgeted at ~1.3-1.8x.

Gate 3 (check-extension-docs.sh) is entirely absent from the dispatch's 'six gates account for virtually all the cost' model, yet measured idle at 124.2s wall (user 61.2s, sys 64.8s) -- the single largest individual gate cost measured in this research, larger than lint-shellcheck.sh's 75.9s. A combined --only-gate run of gates 6,7,9,10,11,21,23 (none individually named as costly by the dispatch) totaled 51.6s, also materially non-free. RECOMMENDATION: add Gate 3 and the gates-6/7/9/10/11/21/23 cluster to the registry's cost-model priority list; its roughly-even user/sys split suggests the lever is reducing per-file subprocess/fork count, not xargs-style parallelization.

Dispatch states the Gate 8 straggler suite (test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh) has '12 nested verify-deploy.sh invocations'; the file on disk has exactly 4, and its own header comment documents it was already optimized from 4 full-battery invocations (~391s) down to 1 full-battery + 3 --only-gate-20-scoped calls (~100s), matching the suite-cost-hints.txt figure of 103000ms the dispatch itself cites. RECOMMENDATION: do not treat straggler invocation-count reduction as a distinct work item; its remaining cost is the one necessary full-battery call and will shrink as the main registry/concurrency work makes full-battery verify-deploy.sh faster.

run-all.sh already contains a mature, well-documented parallel scheduler (opt-in --jobs N|auto, JOBS_CAP=4, longest-first via advisory suite-cost-hints.txt, LOAD_SENSITIVE_BASENAMES serialized set, wait -n worker-slot pool, deterministic discovery-order output, RUN_ALL_NESTED guard) that is directly reusable in shape for verify-deploy.sh's gate-level concurrency. manifest-routing-lib.sh is a proven precedent for the declarative-registry data shape (structured data + one shared sourced interpreter + dedicated lint + dedicated test). RECOMMENDATION: port both patterns directly into the plan rather than designing new mechanisms from scratch.

Confirmed Gate 8's unanchored grep -F '[FAIL]' finding-extraction defect exactly as described in the dispatch (verify-deploy.sh ~line 635). Found the IDENTICAL unanchored pattern at four more call sites feeding gates 6/7/10/11 from four different producers (lint-agent-contracts.sh, lint-routing-wiring.sh, validate-state.sh, lint-contract-compliance.sh), plus a sibling grep -F '[VIOLATION]' pattern at gates 22/23. None of the four siblings currently has a PASS message quoting the scraped token (checked directly), so they are not actively broken today, but share the identical latent defect class. RECOMMENDATION: fix via one shared anchored-extraction helper parameterized by anchor pattern, covering all five+two call sites in the same small Phase 0, not Gate 8 alone.

The dispatch's prescribed anchoring fix (grep -E '^\[FAIL\] ') would silently zero out 12 of the 14 finding-extraction call sites in verify-deploy.sh. Live grep shows 12 of 14 producers emit 'echo -e ${RED}[FAIL]${NC}' / '${RED}[VIOLATION]${NC}' with NO TTY/NO_COLOR guard, so their lines begin with an ANSI SGR escape, not the literal token. Only lint-shellcheck.sh and tests/run-all.sh emit uncolored line-initial tokens. A uniform line-start anchor would therefore convert 12 real gates into silent no-finding gates while appearing to be a hardening fix. The plan must strip SGR before anchoring and prove per-site finding-set equivalence.

The research report's insistence on re-measuring idle paid off directly in planning: it found Gate 3 (check-extension-docs.sh, 124.2s) entirely absent from the dispatch's cost model and larger than the dispatch's headline Gate 22 cost, and showed three gates measured SLOWER idle than contended. That turned into Phase 3, a decision gate that re-derives the cost model mechanically before any scheduling design depends on it, with an explicit contingency descoping the shellcheck phase if the dominant cost turns out to be elsewhere.

gate_registry_exec_concurrent_batch's reconciliation helper (_greg_snapshot_vars) reset its two global associative-array scratch maps via a bare 'NAME=()' assignment. The batch function's own cleanup unset()s those same maps after every call (so a later caller never sees stale baseline data), but unset on a declare -gA variable destroys its type along with its value. On a SECOND call within the same process, the bare 'NAME=()' silently recreated them as ordinary INDEXED arrays. A later string-keyed assignment (MAP["FINDINGS"]=...) on an indexed array evaluates the key ARITHMETICALLY; once the real FINDINGS array already held an element containing a hyphen (e.g. 'finding-1'), bash's arithmetic evaluator parsed that as a subtraction expression and choked on the unset bare identifier before the hyphen, producing a confusing 'finding: unbound variable' crash with no apparent connection to the real defect. Fixed by reasserting 'declare -gA' on every reset instead of a bare '=()' -- caught via a dedicated smoke test that called the batch function twice in the same process, which single-call testing would never have exposed.

gate_registry_exec_concurrent_batch's per-wave worker-cap dispatch loop had an intermittent (~1-in-10 to 1-in-15) cap violation: the longest-first sort used 'mapfile -t _greg_wave_ids < <(... | sort | awk ...)', and the process-substitution pipeline's own background reader could still be unwaited in bash's job table when the dispatch loop's first 'wait -n' ran. That first wait -n would occasionally reap the leftover pipeline reader instead of one of the loop's own backgrounded pool jobs, decrementing the active-worker counter with no real pool job having finished, letting one extra job launch past the declared cap (observed: 3 concurrent jobs at a declared cap of 2). A naive non-atomic read-modify-write test counter could only ever UNDER-count such a violation (never fabricate one), so it masked the bug for several initial test runs; switching the verification counter to flock-guarded atomic increments, then cross-checking with real start/end timestamp overlap, is what exposed it reliably. Fixed with a bare 'wait' immediately after the mapfile/sort pipeline and before the dispatch loop begins, draining the pipeline's own reader before any pool job exists to be confused with it. Confirmed clean across 30/30 isolated repeats and 5/5 full test-suite runs after the fix (2/15 and similar flake rates beforehand).

Phase 8 shellcheck parallelization landed cleanly: default SHELLCHECK_JOBS=8 one-process-per-file worker pool measured 39.5-45.5s vs 76.8-136.4s at SHELLCHECK_JOBS=1 on the real 387-file corpus (host contention varied across runs), a ~1.8-3x win, better than the research's budgeted 1.3-1.8x. Finding-set equivalence verified byte-for-byte against the pre-change original script via a throwaway git worktree, both on the clean real corpus and a seeded SC2155 fixture.

The worker-cap experiment's P=16 continuation was abandoned mid-run when ambient host load spiked to 16+ (1-min load avg) from unrelated concurrent sibling agent sessions on this shared host -- the exact contention hazard this task's own dispatch names. Mitigated by using only the clean P=1/4/8/12 data already collected and by designing the new acceptance test's timing assertion as a relative ratio (parallel <= 80% of forced-single-worker time) rather than an absolute-ms threshold, matching test-run-all-parallel.sh's own prior fix for the identical flakiness class.
